startingHandStrategy.hands: TT, 99, 88, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, AQo
startingHandStrategy.advice: Profitable Open-Raises Across All 6-Max Positions; Exercise Caution Facing 4-Bets Out Of Position.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: Speculative Suited Connectors & Wheel Aces
startingHandStrategy.advice: High Implied-Odds Hands That Thrive In Late Position And Deep-Stacked Pots Or As Polarized 3-Bet Bluffs (A5s/A4s).

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: Serves As The Baseline Benchmark Variant Against Which All Other Poker Formats Are Measured.
Unlike Omaha Variants, Players Are Never Required To Use Exactly Two Hole Cards And Can Play One Hole Card Or The Entire Five-Card Board.
Features 1,326 Total Starting Combinations Grouped Into 169 Canonical Starting Hands (13 Pocket Pairs, 78 Suited Hands, And 78 Offsuit Hands).

faqs.q: How Many Starting Hand Combinations Exist In Texas Hold'em?
faqs.a: From A 52-Card Deck, There Are Exactly (52 x 51) / 2 = 1,326 Specific Two-Card Combinations, Which Condense Into 169 Strategic Starting Hands: 13 Pocket Pairs (6 Combos Each), 78 Suited Hands (4 Combos Each), And 78 Offsuit Hands (12 Combos Each).

faqs.q: Does A Single High Card In My Hand Break A Tie If The Board Has Four Of A Kind?
faqs.a: Only If Your Hole Card Is Higher Than Both The Fifth Board Card And Your Opponent's Hole Cards. Because Poker Hands Are Strictly Five Cards Long, Four Of A Kind On The Board Plus An Ace On The Board Cannot Be Improved By Any Pocket Pair.

pokerVariants.name: Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO4)
pokerVariants.title: 4-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO4) Rules, Must-Use-Two Rule & Strategy
pokerVariants.h1: 4-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO4) Official Rules, Pot Calculation, And Nut-Draw Strategy
pokerVariants.holeCards: 4 Face-Down Hole Cards (MUST Use Exactly 2 Hole Cards)
pokerVariants.boardCards: 5 Community Cards (MUST Use Exactly 3 Board Cards)
pokerVariants.bettingStructure: Pot-Limit (Maximum Bet = 3x Facing Bet + Trail + Center Pot)
pokerVariants.summary: 4-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO4) Deals Each Player Four Private Hole Cards And Five Community Cards, Requiring Every Player To Use Exactly Two Of Their Hole Cards And Exactly Three Board Cards To Make Their 5-Card Hand.
rulesOverview: Each Player Is Dealt Four Private Hole Cards Face Down, Creating 6 Distinct Two-Card Combinations Inside Every Hand (C(4,2) = 6).
Mandatory Two-Card Rule: At Showdown, Every Player Must Use Exactly 2 Of Their 4 Hole Cards Combined With Exactly 3 Of The 5 Community Cards - Never 1 Hole Card And Never 3 Hole Cards.
Betting Is Governed By Pot-Limit Rules: The Minimum Bet Is One Big Blind And The Maximum Raise Equals The Total Pot After Calling (3x The Facing Bet Plus Trail Bets Plus Center Pot).
Because Every Hand Contains Six Two-Card Combos, Preflop Equities Run Close Together (Pocket Aces Are Only A 53% To 65% Favorite Against Connected Rundowns).

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: Double-Suited Aces & High Pairs
startingHandStrategy.hands: A-A-K-K Double-Suited, A-A-J-T Double-Suited, A-A-Q-Q Double-Suited
startingHandStrategy.advice: Play Aggressively With 3-Bets And 4-Bets To Lower The Postflop Stack-To-Pot Ratio (SPR) And Commit On The Flop.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: High-Card Broadway & Connected Rundowns
startingHandStrategy.hands: K-Q-J-T Double-Suited, Q-J-T-9 Double-Suited, J-T-9-8 Double-Suited
startingHandStrategy.advice: Elite Postflop Playability Capable Of Flopping 13-Out, 17-Out, And 20-Out Nut Straight Wrap Draws.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: Danglers, Rainbow Disconnected Hands & Quadruple Pocket Cards
startingHandStrategy.hands: K-9-5-2 Rainbow, A-A-A-7 (Trips In Hand), Non-Nut Single-Suited Hands
startingHandStrategy.advice: Fold Immediately Preflop; Drawing To Non-Nut Flushes Or Holding Three Of The Same Rank In Your Hand Cripples Your Outs.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: You Must Always Use Exactly Two Hole Cards And Three Board Cards (Holding A Single Spade On A Four-Spade Board Does NOT Make A Flush).
Preflop Hand Equities Are Compressed Within A Narrow 60/40 Window, Shifting Strategy Toward Multi-Draw Nut Redraws And Wrap Equity.
Contains C(52,4) = 270,725 Total Starting Hand Combinations Compared To Only 1,326 In Texas Hold'em.

faqs.q: If The Board Has Four Hearts And I Hold Only The Ace Of Hearts, Do I Have A Flush In PLO?
faqs.a: No. Because PLO Requires You To Use Exactly Two Hole Cards And Three Board Cards, You Must Hold At Least Two Hearts In Your Hand To Make A Flush.

faqs.q: What Is A 20-Out Wrap Draw In Pot-Limit Omaha?
faqs.a: When You Hold Four Consecutive Cards Around Two Connected Flop Cards (Such As Q-J-8-7 On A T-9-2 Flop), Any Queen, Jack, Eight, Or Seven Completes A Straight, Giving You 16 To 20 Unseen Straight Outs.

pokerVariants.name: 5-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO5)
pokerVariants.title: 5-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO5) Rules, 10-Combo Math & Strategy
pokerVariants.h1: 5-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO5) Official Rules, Equity Compression, And Nut Advantage
pokerVariants.holeCards: 5 Face-Down Hole Cards (MUST Use Exactly 2 Hole Cards)
pokerVariants.boardCards: 5 Community Cards (MUST Use Exactly 3 Board Cards)
pokerVariants.summary: 5-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO5) Deals Five Private Hole Cards To Each Player While Preserving The Strict Omaha Rule That Exactly Two Hole Cards And Three Community Cards Must Be Used At Showdown.
rulesOverview: Each Player Receives Five Private Hole Cards, Generating C(5,2) = 10 Distinct Two-Card Combinations Per Player (67% More Combos Than 4-Card PLO).
Despite Holding Five Cards, Players Must Still Use Exactly 2 Hole Cards And 3 Board Cards At Showdown.
By The Pidgeonhole Principle, Every 5-Card Hand Is Guaranteed To Contain At Least One Suited Combination Across The Four Suits, And Can Be At Most Double-Suited.
Because 5 Cards Per Player Consume 30 Cards In A 6-Max Game Plus 5 Board Cards And 3 Burns (38 Cards), PLO5 Is Capped At 6 Or 7 Players Maximum.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: Double-Suited Nut Ace + High Pair + Rundown Side Cards
startingHandStrategy.hands: A-A-K-Q-J Double-Suited, A-K-Q-J-T Double-Suited With Nut Suit
startingHandStrategy.advice: Prioritize Hands Featuring An Ace-High Flush Suit Paired With High Connected Side Cards That Dominate Multiway Pots.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: Five-Card Connected Rundowns With Nut Suit
startingHandStrategy.hands: Q-J-T-9-8 Double-Suited, K-Q-J-T-8 With Ace Side Suit
startingHandStrategy.advice: Frequently Flops Monster Straight Wraps Plus Flush Redraws That Are Mathematical Favorites Even Against Naked Overpairs.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: Naked Aces With Duplicate Ranks Or Non-Nut Suits
startingHandStrategy.hands: A-A-8-8-8, K-K-Q-6-2 Single-Suited
startingHandStrategy.advice: Avoid Overplaying Naked A-A Without Strong Side Connectivity; Bare Top Set Without Redraws Frequently Faces 55%+ Equity Wraps.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: Ten Internal Two-Card Combinations Per Hand Mean Naked Top Set Or Bare Non-Nut Flushes Are Frequently Drawing Thin Or Dead.
Holdings With A-x Flush Blockers Gain Enormous Bluffing Leverage Because Five Cards Per Player Make Card Removal Twice As Pronounced.
Contains C(52,5) = 2,598,960 Possible 5-Card Starting Hands.

faqs.q: Can A 5-Card Omaha Hand Be Triple-Suited?
faqs.a: No. Because A Suited Combination Requires At Least Two Cards Of The Same Suit, Five Hole Cards Can At Most Form Two Distinct Pairs Of Suits (2 + 2 + 1), Making Double-Suited The Maximum Possible.

faqs.q: Why Is Top Two Pair Or Bare Top Set Much Weaker In PLO5 Than In PLO4?
faqs.a: With 10 Two-Card Combinations Per Player Instead Of 6, Opponents Flop Straight Wraps Coupled With Nut Flush Draws Far More Often, Requiring You To Hold Backdoor Flush Or Higher Boat Redraws To Continue.

pokerVariants.name: 6-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO6)
pokerVariants.title: 6-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO6) Rules, 15-Combo Math & Max Table Cap
pokerVariants.h1: 6-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO6) Official Rules, 15-Combo Dynamics, And Triple-Suited Hands
pokerVariants.holeCards: 6 Face-Down Hole Cards (MUST Use Exactly 2 Hole Cards)
pokerVariants.boardCards: 5 Community Cards (MUST Use Exactly 3 Board Cards)
pokerVariants.bettingStructure: Pot-Limit (Capped At 6-Max Or 5-Max Due To 52-Card Deck Limit)
pokerVariants.summary: 6-Card Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO6) Deals Six Private Hole Cards To Each Player (15 Internal Two-Card Combinations) While Still Enforcing The Exact Two-Hole-Card And Three-Board-Card Rule.
rulesOverview: Every Player Receives Six Private Hole Cards, Giving Each Hand C(6,2) = 15 Internal Two-Card Combinations.
At Showdown, Every Player Must Still Select Exactly 2 Of Their 6 Hole Cards And 3 Of The 5 Community Cards.
Unlike PLO4 And PLO5, A 6-Card Hand Can Be Triple-Suited (Two Cards In Each Of Three Different Suits: 2 + 2 + 2).
Deck Exhaustion Cap: 6 Players x 6 Hole Cards (36) + 5 Board Cards + 3 Burn Cards = 44 Cards Used Out Of 52, Strictly Limiting Tables To 6-Max Maximum.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: Triple-Suited Aces With Broadway Rundown
startingHandStrategy.hands: A-A-K-Q-J-T Triple-Suited, A-K-Q-J-T-9 With Two Nut Suits
startingHandStrategy.advice: Maximum Preflop Equity And Nut Redraw Coverage Across Virtually Every Flop Texture.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: Nut-Suit Six-Card Rundowns
startingHandStrategy.hands: K-Q-J-T-9-8 With Ace-High Flush Suit
startingHandStrategy.advice: Dominates Multiway Flops By Flopping Both Ends Of Straight Wraps And Backdoor Nut Flushes.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: Paired-Out Or Low-Suit Cluttered Hands
startingHandStrategy.hands: J-J-J-6-6-2, 9-8-7-4-3-2 Without Nut Suit
startingHandStrategy.advice: Fold Immediately; In PLO6, Any Hand That Cannot Make The Absolute Nuts Plus A Redraw Is A Reverse-Implied-Odds Trap.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: With 15 Two-Card Combinations Per Player, Somebody Almost Always Holds The Exact Nuts On Every Street.
Card Removal (Blockers) Is Massive: Seeing 6 Cards In Your Own Hand Plus 5 On The Board Accounts For 21% Of The Entire Deck.
Contains C(52,6) = 20,358,520 Distinct 6-Card Starting Hands.

faqs.q: Why Can't 6-Card Omaha Be Played At A Full 8-Handed Or 9-Handed Table?
faqs.a: An 8-Handed Table Would Require 48 Hole Cards Plus 5 Board Cards And 3 Burn Cards = 56 Cards, Exceeding A Standard 52-Card Deck. Therefore, PLO6 Is Strictly Capped At 6 Players.

faqs.q: Can I Use Three Hole Cards In 6-Card Omaha Since I Have Six Cards?
faqs.a: Never. Whether You Play PLO4, PLO5, Or PLO6, Every Omaha Variant Strictly Requires Using Exactly 2 Hole Cards And 3 Community Cards.

pokerVariants.name: Omaha Hi-Lo 8-Or-Better (PLO8 / O8)
pokerVariants.title: Omaha Hi-Lo 8-Or-Better (PLO8 & Limit O8) Rules, Qualifier & Strategy
pokerVariants.h1: Omaha Hi-Lo 8-Or-Better (PLO8 / O8) Rules: Split-Pot Qualifier And Scoop Strategy
pokerVariants.holeCards: 4 Face-Down Hole Cards (Independent 2-Card Selection For High And Low)
pokerVariants.summary: Omaha Hi-Lo 8-Or-Better Splits The Pot 50/50 Between The Best High Hand And The Best Qualifying 8-Or-Better Low Hand (Five Unpaired Cards 8 Or Lower), Using Independent Two-Hole-Card Combinations For Each Half.
rulesOverview: Each Player Receives 4 Hole Cards And Must Use Exactly 2 Hole Cards + 3 Board Cards For High, And May Use The Same Or A Completely Different Pair Of Hole Cards + 3 Board Cards For Low.

8-Or-Better Low Qualifier: To Qualify For The Low Half Of The Pot, The Board Must Contain At Least Three Unpaired Cards Ranked 8 Or Lower (Ace Counts As 1), And The Player Must Make Five Unpaired Cards 8 Or Lower.
Straights And Flushes Do Not Count Against A Low Hand, Making A-2-3-4-5 ("The Wheel") The Best Possible Low Hand As Well As A 5-High Straight.
If Fewer Than Three Unpaired Cards 8 Or Lower Appear On The Board, No Low Hand Is Possible And The Best High Hand Scoops 100% Of The Pot.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: Nut Low + Nut High Two-Way Scoop Hands
startingHandStrategy.hands: A-A-2-3 Double-Suited, A-A-2-K Double-Suited, A-2-3-K Double-Suited
startingHandStrategy.advice: The Gold Standard Of O8: Capable Of Making The Nut A-2 Low With Counterfeit Protection (A-3) Plus Nut Flushes And Top Set For High.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: Protected Wheel Wraps With Suited Ace
startingHandStrategy.hands: A-2-4-Q Suited Ace, A-2-3-5 Suited, A-3-4-5 Double-Suited
startingHandStrategy.advice: Strong Multiway Playability Aiming To Free-Roll Or Three-Quarter Opponents Who Hold Naked A-2 Without Backup.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: Middle Cards & One-Way High-Only Hands
startingHandStrategy.hands: 9-8-7-6, K-Q-J-9 Offsuit, A-5-8-9 (Weak Low)
startingHandStrategy.advice: Fold Immediately; Middle Cards (6-7-8-9) Make The Worst Lows And The Lowest Straights, Guaranteeing You Get Quartered Or Scooped.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: Playing Only For Half The Pot With A Naked Low Draw Risks Getting "Quartered" (Tying The Low For 25% Of The Pot After Putting In 50% Of The Money).
Counterfeiting Occurs When A Board Card Pairs One Of Your Critical Low Hole Cards (Such As Pairing Your Deuce When You Hold A-2-K-K).
The Odd Chip In Any Split Pot Always Goes To The Winning High Hand.

faqs.q: What Does Getting "Quartered" Mean In Omaha Hi-Lo?
faqs.a: If You And An Opponent Both Hold Ace-Deuce For The Exact Same Nut Low While Your Opponent Also Wins The High Hand, Your Opponent Wins 75% Of The Pot (50% High + 25% Tied Low) And You Only Receive 25% ("One Quarter"), Resulting In A Net Chip Loss.

faqs.q: Does A Flush Or Straight Disqualify My Low Hand In Omaha 8-Or-Better?
faqs.a: No. Omaha Hi-Lo Uses Ace-To-Five (California) Lowball Rules Where Straights And Flushes Are Completely Ignored When Evaluating Low Hands.

pokerVariants.name: Short Deck (6+ Hold'em)
pokerVariants.title: Short Deck (6+ Hold'em) Rules, 36-Card Rankings & Equity Math
pokerVariants.h1: Short Deck (6+ Hold'Em) Official Rules: Why Flush Beats Full House & Button Blind Format
pokerVariants.holeCards: 2 Face-Down Hole Cards (36-Card Deck: 2s, 3s, 4s, And 5s Removed)
pokerVariants.bettingStructure: No-Limit Ante-Only Format With Double Button Blind
pokerVariants.handRankingSystem: Short Deck Rankings: Flush Beats Full House; A-6-7-8-9 Is The Low Straight
pokerVariants.summary: Short Deck (6+ Hold'em) Strips All 2s, 3s, 4s, And 5s From The Deck To Play With 36 Cards, Causing Flushes To Outrank Full Houses And Aces To Play As Both The High Card And The 5 In A-6-7-8-9 Straights.
rulesOverview: Deck Composition: All 16 Cards Ranked 2, 3, 4, And 5 Are Removed, Leaving 36 Total Cards (9 Ranks From 6 Through Ace Across 4 Suits).
Adjusted Hand Rankings: Because Only 9 Cards Of Each Suit Exist, A Flush (Only 4,140 Combos) Is Rarer And Beats A Full House (12,960 Combos).
Ace-Low Straight Rule: The Ace Plays High In A-K-Q-J-T And Also Substitutes For The Missing 5 To Form The Lowest Straight: A-6-7-8-9 (A 9-High Straight).
Ante + Button Blind Structure: Every Player Posts 1 Ante Unit And The Dealer Button Posts An Additional "Button Blind"; Action Starts Left Of The Button On Every Street.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: High Pocket Pairs & Suited Broadways
startingHandStrategy.hands: AA, KK, QQ, AKs, AKo, KQs
startingHandStrategy.advice: Strongest Preflop Holdings, Though Even Pocket Aces Have Narrower Equity Edges Against Connected Hands Than In 52-Card Hold'em.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: Connected Mid-Rundowns & Suited Connectors
startingHandStrategy.hands: JTs, T9s, 98s, 87s, 76s, QJs
startingHandStrategy.advice: In A 36-Card Deck, Open-Ended Straight Draws (8 Outs) Have Roughly 48% To 50% Equity On The Flop Using The Rule Of 6 And 3.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: Offsuit Disconnected High-Low Gappers
startingHandStrategy.hands: K6o, Q6o, J6o, A7o
startingHandStrategy.advice: Dominated Hands That Frequently Make Second-Best Pairs Or Non-Nut Straights.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: A Flush Officially Beats A Full House Because Only 9 Cards Of Each Suit Exist In The 36-Card Deck.
Use The "Rule Of 6 And 3" Instead Of The Rule Of 4 And 2: Each Out Is Worth ~3.2% Per Street (8-Out Straight Draw = ~48% Equity On The Flop).
Contains Only C(36,2) = 630 Total Two-Card Combos Across 81 Canonical Starting Hands (9x9 Matrix).

faqs.q: Why Does A Flush Beat A Full House In Short Deck Poker?
faqs.a: Out Of C(36,5) = 376,992 Possible 5-Card Hands In A 36-Card Deck, There Are 12,960 Full Houses But Only 4,104 Flushes (Plus 36 Straight Flushes), Making A Flush More Than Three Times Rarer Than A Full House.

faqs.q: What Is The Lowest Straight In Short Deck 6+ Hold'em?
faqs.a: A-6-7-8-9 Is The Lowest Straight (A 9-High Straight), Because The Ace Steps In Where The Removed 5 Would Normally Sit.

pokerVariants.name: Double-Board PLO Bomb Pots
pokerVariants.title: Double-Board PLO Bomb Pot Rules, Split-Pot Math & Scoop Strategy
pokerVariants.h1: Double-Board Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO) Bomb Pot Rules And Two-Board Strategy
pokerVariants.holeCards: 4 Or 5 Face-Down Hole Cards (Must Use 2 Hole Cards Independently On Each Board)
pokerVariants.boardCards: Two Separate 5-Card Boards Dealt Simultaneously (10 Community Cards Total)
pokerVariants.bettingStructure: Pre-Flop Ante Only (No Preflop Betting), Then Pot-Limit Across Flop, Turn & River
pokerVariants.handRankingSystem: 50% Top Board High Hand / 50% Bottom Board High Hand
pokerVariants.summary: In A Double-Board PLO Bomb Pot, Every Player Posts A Uniform Ante And Skips Preflop Betting To See Two Simultaneous 3-Card Flops, Playing One Central Pot Split 50/50 Between The Top Board And Bottom Board.
rulesOverview: All Participating Players Post An Agreed Bomb Pot Ante (Typically 2BB To 5BB) And Hole Cards Are Dealt With Zero Preflop Betting Round.
The Dealer Immediately Burns One Card And Deals Two Parallel 3-Card Flops (Top Board And Bottom Board), Followed By Simultaneous Turn And River Cards.
There Is Only One Central Pot And One Betting Action Per Street Starting Left Of The Dealer Button; Any Bet Applies To Both Boards At Once.
At Showdown, Players Use Any Two Of Their Hole Cards With Three Top-Board Cards For Top Half (50%) And Any Two Of Their Hole Cards With Three Bottom-Board Cards For Bottom Half (50%).

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: Nut Lock On One Board + Strong Draw On Second Board
startingHandStrategy.hands: Top Set Or Nut Flush/Straight On Board A + Nut Draw Or Two Pair On Board B
startingHandStrategy.advice: This Is A "Freeroll" Position: Pot And Re-Pot Aggressively Because You Cannot Lose Money And Can Scoop 100% Of The Pot.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: Strong Draws On Both Boards Simultaneously
startingHandStrategy.hands: Nut Flush Draw On Top Board + Open-Ended Wrap On Bottom Board
startingHandStrategy.advice: Play Semi-Bluff Raises When Holding Shared Ace Or Broadway Blockers That Reduce Opponents' Ability To Hold Lock Nuts.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: One-Board Non-Nut Hand With Zero Equity On The Other Board
startingHandStrategy.hands: Middle Set Or Queen-High Flush On Board A + Complete Air On Board B
startingHandStrategy.advice: Fold Facing Multi-Street Pot-Sized Bets; Paying Three Streets To At Best Chop 50% Of The Pot Is A Massive Long-Term EV Bleed.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: Skipping Preflop Action Means Every Single Player Reaches The Flop With 100% Random Unfiltered Ranges (7-2-4-9 Appears Just As Often As A-A-K-K).
Winning Only One Board Merely Returns Your Own Postflop Bets Minus Rake; Real Profit Comes Strictly From Scooping Both Boards Or Three-Quartering.
In 5-Card Double-Board PLO With 6 Players, 30 Hole Cards + 10 Board Cards + 3 Burns = 43 Of 52 Cards Are In Play.

faqs.q: Do I Have To Use The Same Two Hole Cards On Both The Top And Bottom Boards?
faqs.a: No. Each Board Is Evaluated Completely Independently: You Can Use Hole Cards 1 And 2 To Make A Full House On The Top Board, And Hole Cards 3 And 4 To Make A Flush On The Bottom Board.

faqs.q: Who Gets The Odd Chip In A Double-Board Bomb Pot?
faqs.a: When The Total Pot Cannot Be Divided Evenly Into Two Identical Halves, The Single Odd Chip Is Always Awarded To The Winner Of The Top (Upper) Board.

pokerVariants.name: Seven-Card Stud High
pokerVariants.title: Seven-Card Stud High Rules, Bring-In, Streets & Strategy
pokerVariants.h1: Seven-Card Stud Official Rules: Third Through Seventh Street, Bring-In, And Dead Cards
pokerVariants.holeCards: 3 Face-Down Cards (2 On Third Street + 1 On Seventh Street)
pokerVariants.boardCards: 4 Face-Up Exposed Door/Upcards Per Player (No Shared Community Cards)
pokerVariants.bettingStructure: Fixed-Limit With Antes And Forced Low-Card Bring-In On Third Street
pokerVariants.summary: Seven-Card Stud Is A Non-Community-Card Fixed-Limit Game Where Each Player Receives Seven Individual Cards Across Five Betting Streets (Two Down, Four Up, One Down) And Makes Their Best 5-Card High Hand.
rulesOverview: Third Street Deal & Bring-In: All Players Post An Ante And Receive Two Face-Down Hole Cards Plus One Face-Up "Door Card". The Player With The Lowest Door Card (By Rank, Then Suit: Clubs Lowest, Diamonds, Hearts, Spades) Must Post The Forced Bring-In Or Complete To A Full Small Bet.

Fourth, Fifth, And Sixth Streets: Each Active Player Receives One Additional Face-Up Card Per Street. Starting On Fourth Street, Action Always Begins With The Player Showing The Highest Exposed Poker Hand.
Double Bet Transition: Third And Fourth Streets Use The Small Bet Limit (Except In Optional Pair-On-Fourth-Street Rules); Fifth, Sixth, And Seventh Streets Use The Big Bet Limit.
Seventh Street (The River): Each Player Receives Their Seventh And Final Card Face Down ("Down And Dirty"), Followed By The Final Betting Round And Showdown.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: Rolled-Up Trips & High Split/Wired Pairs With Live Kickers
startingHandStrategy.hands: (A-A)A, (K-K)K, (A-A)K, (K-Q)K With All Suits And Ranks Live
startingHandStrategy.advice: Complete Or Raise Immediately On Third Street To Thin The Field And Extract Maximum Value.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: Three-Flushes & Three-Card Straight Connectors With Live Outs
startingHandStrategy.hands: (A-Q)T All Spades, (J-T)9 Rainbow With Zero Dead Tens Or Eights Seen
startingHandStrategy.advice: Profitable Only When Most Of Your Suit And Rank Cards Remain Unseen Across Opponents' Exposed Door Cards.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: Dead-Out Pairs & Dominated Low Pairs
startingHandStrategy.hands: (8-8)3 When Two Eights Are Already Folded Face Up Around The Table
startingHandStrategy.advice: Fold Immediately; In Stud, Tracking Exposed Dead Upcards Is The Single Most Important Skill.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: There Is No Dealer Button And No Community Board: Action Order Changes On Every Street Based On Who Shows The Highest Exposed Upcards.
Bridge Suit Order (Spades High > Hearts > Diamonds > Clubs Low) Determines Both The Mandatory Third-Street Bring-In And Who Acts First When Exposed Upcards Tie.
If An 8-Player Hand Runs Out Of Cards Before Seventh Street, The Dealer Deals One Shared Community Card Face Up In The Center For All Remaining Players.

faqs.q: Which Suit Has To Post The Bring-In When Two Players Tie For The Lowest Door Card In Stud?
faqs.a: Alphabetical Bridge Suit Order Breaks All Door-Card Ties From Lowest To Highest: Clubs (Lowest), Diamonds, Hearts, And Spades (Highest). Therefore, A 2 Of Clubs Must Post The Bring-In Over A 2 Of Diamonds.

faqs.q: What Does "Rolled Up" Mean In Seven-Card Stud?
faqs.a: Being Dealt Three Of A Kind On Your Very First Three Cards On Third Street (Two Down And One Up) Is Called Being "Rolled Up", Which Occurs Once Every 425 Hands (0.24%).

pokerVariants.name: Seven-Card Stud Hi-Lo 8-Or-Better
pokerVariants.title: Seven-Card Stud Hi-Lo 8-Or-Better (Stud8) Rules & Strategy
pokerVariants.h1: Seven-Card Stud Hi-Lo 8-Or-Better (Stud8) Official Rules And Two-Way Scoop Strategy
pokerVariants.holeCards: 3 Face-Down Cards (2 On Third Street + 1 On Seventh Street)
pokerVariants.bettingStructure: Fixed-Limit With Antes And Low-Card Bring-In
pokerVariants.summary: Seven-Card Stud Hi-Lo 8-Or-Better (Stud8) Combines Five-Street Seven-Card Stud Mechanics With An 8-Or-Better Split Pot, Where The Best High Hand And Best Qualifying Low Hand Split The Pot 50/50.
rulesOverview: Uses The Same Seven-Card Deal As Stud High (2 Down + 1 Up On Third Street, Upcards On Fourth/Fifth/Sixth, And Final Card Down On Seventh).
The Lowest Door Card By Rank And Bridge Suit Order Posts The Bring-In On Third Street (With Aces Counting As High For Door-Card Bring-In Purposes).
From Fourth Street Through Seventh Street, The Player Showing The Highest Exposed High Poker Hand Always Acts First.
At Showdown, Any Five Of A Player's Seven Cards Form Their High Hand And Any Five Cards Form Their 8-Or-Better Low Hand; If Nobody Makes Five Unpaired Cards 8 Or Lower, The High Hand Scoops.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: Ace-Low Three-Flushes & Ace-Low Pairs With Low Door Card
startingHandStrategy.hands: (A-2)3 All Hearts, (A-A)2, (A-3)5 Suited With Live Low Cards
startingHandStrategy.advice: Elite Two-Way Hands That Threaten Both A Wheel Low And A Flush Or Aces-Up High To Scoop The Entire Pot.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: Three Unpaired Wheel Cards Or Rolled-Up Trips
startingHandStrategy.hands: (2-4)5 Rainbow With Live Aces/Threes, (K-K)K Rolled Up
startingHandStrategy.advice: Playable When Low Cards Around The Table Are Live Or When Your High Hand Can Prevent Opponents From Making A Low.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: High-Only One-Way Pairs & Rough 8-High Lows
startingHandStrategy.hands: (Q-Q)4, (8-7)6 Rainbow With Dead Low Cards
startingHandStrategy.advice: Fold On Third Street Whenever Multiple Low Door Cards Are Out Against A High Pair.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: Unlike Omaha Hi-Lo Where Everyone Shares One Board, In Stud8 One Player Can Clearly Show Four Low Upcards While Another Shows High Pairs.
There Is No Fourth-Street Double-Bet Option For An Exposed Pair In Stud Hi-Lo (Third And Fourth Streets Always Use The Small Bet).
Scooping Both Halves Of The Pot By Holding A Low That Also Completes A Straight Or Flush Is The Core Path To Profit.

faqs.q: Does An Ace Door Card Count As High Or Low For The Third-Street Bring-In In Stud8?
faqs.a: Even Though Aces Play Both High And Low At Showdown, An Exposed Ace On Third Street Always Counts As The Highest Rank For Door-Card Purposes And Never Posts The Low Bring-In.

faqs.q: Can I Use Different Five-Card Subsets Of My Seven Cards For High And Low?
faqs.a: Yes. Out Of Your Seven Final Cards, You Choose Your Best 5-Card High Hand And Independently Choose Your Best 5-Card Low Hand.

pokerVariants.name: Razz (Seven-Card Lowball)
pokerVariants.title: Razz Poker Rules: Seven-Card Ace-To-Five Lowball Rankings & Strategy
pokerVariants.h1: Razz Poker Official Rules: Seven-Card Ace-To-Five Lowball, High-Card Bring-In & Wheel Rankings
pokerVariants.holeCards: 3 Face-Down Cards (2 On Third Street + 1 On Seventh Street)
pokerVariants.bettingStructure: Fixed-Limit With Antes And HIGH-Card Bring-In On Third Street
pokerVariants.summary: Razz Is Seven-Card Stud Played Strictly For The Lowest 5-Card Ace-To-Five Hand (Where Aces Are Always Low, Straights And Flushes Do Not Count Against You, And A-2-3-4-5 Is The Unbeatable Wheel).
rulesOverview: Reverse Bring-In: On Third Street, The Player With The HIGHEST Exposed Door Card (King High, With Spades Highest For Ties, Because Aces Are Low) Must Post The Forced Bring-In.
From Fourth Street Onward, The Player Showing The Best (LOWEST) Exposed Upcards Acts First On Every Betting Round.

Ace-To-Five Lowball Ranking: Aces Are Always The Lowest Card (1), Straights And Flushes Do Not Hurt Your Low, And Low Hands Are Read Top-Down From Their Highest Card (For Example, 7-5-4-2-A Beats 7-6-3-2-A).
The Entire Pot Is Awarded 100% To The Best 5-Card Low Hand Made From Each Player's 7 Cards, With No 8-Or-Better Qualifier Required.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: Three Wheel Cards (5 Or Lower) With Low Door Card
startingHandStrategy.hands: (A-2)3, (A-3)4, (2-3)5 With Live Low Ranks Around The Table
startingHandStrategy.advice: Complete And Raise Aggressively On Third Street To Isolate High-Door-Card Bring-Ins And Steal Antes.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: Smooth 6-Low Or 7-Low Starters In Steal Position
startingHandStrategy.hands: (A-2)6, (2-4)7, (A-4)7 When Folded To Late Action With High Cards Behind
startingHandStrategy.advice: Strong Steal And Continuation Hands When Opponents Catch Bricks (9, T, J, Q, K) On Fourth Street.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: Rough 8-Highs Or Concealed Pairs
startingHandStrategy.hands: (3-8)2, (A-A)4, (4-7)8 With Dead Low Cards
startingHandStrategy.advice: Fold Immediately On Third Street; Drawing To An 8-7 Low Against Smooth 6-Low Or 7-Low Upcards Is Heavily Dominated.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: Aces Are Strictly Low (1), Suits And Straights Never Matter For Hand Strength, And The Highest Door Card (King Of Spades Worst) Posts The Bring-In.
Low Hands Are Evaluated By Their Highest Card Downward: A "Smooth Eight" (8-5-3-2-A) Crushes A "Rough Eight" (8-7-6-4-2).
Seeing Your Opponents Brick Out With Paint Cards (J, Q, K) On Fourth Or Fifth Street Allows Automatic Value Bets Even When Your Own Hand Pairs.

faqs.q: Which Hand Wins Between 8-4-3-2-A And 7-6-5-4-3 In Razz?
faqs.a: 7-6-5-4-3 Wins! Even Though 7-6-5-4-3 Is A 7-High Straight In Hold'em, Straights Do Not Count In Razz, And A 7-High Low Always Beats An 8-High Low.

faqs.q: Which Suit Posts The Bring-In When Two Players Show A King On Third Street In Razz?
faqs.a: Because The Worst (Highest) Card Posts The Bring-In In Razz, Standard Bridge Suit Order Applies: The King Of Spades Is Higher (Worse) Than The King Of Hearts, Diamonds, Or Clubs And Must Post The Bring-In.

pokerVariants.name: 2-7 Triple Draw Lowball
pokerVariants.title: 2-7 Triple Draw Lowball (Kansas City Lowball) Rules & 7-5-4-3-2 Rankings
pokerVariants.h1: 2-7 Triple Draw Lowball (Kansas City Lowball) Official Rules, Three Draws & Strategy
pokerVariants.holeCards: 5 Private Cards Per Player With 3 Sequential Draw Opportunities
pokerVariants.bettingStructure: Fixed-Limit Across 4 Betting Rounds (Before Draw 1, After Draw 1, After Draw 2, After Draw 3)
pokerVariants.handRankingSystem: Deuce-To-Seven (Kansas City) Lowball: Aces Are HIGH, Straights & Flushes Hurt (7-5-4-3-2 Offsuit Is The Nuts)
pokerVariants.summary: 2-7 Triple Draw (Kansas City Lowball) Is A Fixed-Limit Closed Draw Game With Three Card-Exchange Rounds Where Aces Always Count As High Cards And Straights And Flushes Count Against Your Low, Making 7-5-4-3-2 Unsuited ("The Wheel" / "Number One") The Best Possible Hand.
rulesOverview: Uses A Dealer Button, Small Blind, And Big Blind With Four Fixed-Limit Betting Rounds Interleaved With Three Draw Rounds (Small Bet Before And After Draw 1; Big Bet After Draw 2 And Draw 3).
On Each Of The Three Draws, Active Players May Discard Anywhere From 1 To 5 Cards To Receive Replacements From The Deck, Or "Stand Pat" (Discard 0 Cards).

Deuce-To-Seven Hand Rankings: Exact Opposite Of High Poker. Aces Are Always HIGH (So A-2-3-4-5 Is NOT A Low Straight - It Is Simply Ace-High, Which Loses To Every Unpaired King-High Or Better), And Straights And Flushes Count Against You.
The Best Possible Hand Is 7-5-4-3-2 Not All Of The Same Suit ("Number One"), Followed By 7-6-4-3-2, 7-6-5-3-2, 7-6-5-4-2, And 8-5-4-3-2.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 1: Pat 7-Lows, Pat Smooth 8-Lows & One-Card Draws To A 7
startingHandStrategy.advice: Raise And 3-Bet From Every Position; One-Card Draws Containing A Deuce Have Massive Equity Over Three Draws.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 2: Two-Card Wheel Draws Containing A Deuce
startingHandStrategy.advice: Strong Open-Raises From Middle And Late Position; Always Prioritize Keeping A Deuce To Avoid Making Accidental Straights.

startingHandStrategy.tier: Tier 3: Three-Card Draws & Straight-Prone Non-Deuce Draws
startingHandStrategy.hands: 3-4-5-6-x (Open-Ended Straight Trap), 4-5-6-x-x, Any Hand With Aces
startingHandStrategy.advice: Fold Preflop; Holding 3-4-5-6 Means Every 2 Or 7 You Catch Makes A Straight Instead Of A Low.

keyDifferencesFromHoldem: Aces Are Strictly High Cards And Straights/Flushes Destroy Your Low Hand (Making 7-5-4-3-2 Offsuit The Nuts Instead Of A-2-3-4-5).
Because There Are Zero Exposed Cards, Information Comes Entirely From Position, Betting Action, And How Many Cards Each Opponent Draws (1, 2, 3, Or Standing Pat).
In Multiway Hands, The Deck Can Run Out Of Cards On The Third Draw, Requiring Previously Mucked Discards And Burn Cards To Be Reshuffled.

faqs.q: Why Is 7-5-4-3-2 The Best Hand In 2-7 Lowball Instead Of 6-5-4-3-2?
faqs.a: Because 6-5-4-3-2 Is A Six-High Straight! In Deuce-To-Seven Lowball, Straights And Flushes Count Against You As High Hands, So 7-5-4-3-2 Unsuited Is The Lowest Possible 5-Card Combination Without A Straight.

faqs.q: Is A-2-3-4-5 A Straight In Deuce-To-Seven Lowball?
faqs.a: No. In 2-7 Rules, The Ace Plays Strictly High (Above A King) And Never Counts As A 1, So A-5-4-3-2 Unsuited Is Simply An Ace-High Unpaired Hand (Which Still Beats One Pair, Straights, And Flushes, But Loses To Any King-High Or Better).

faqs.q: What Does "Snowing" Mean In No-Limit 2-7 Single Draw?
faqs.a: Snowing Is Standing Pat (Drawing Zero Cards) With A Garbage Hand Like Two Pair Or Three Aces With The Intention Of Firing A Large Post-Draw Bluff If Your Drawing Opponent Bricks Their 1-Card Draw.

faqs.q: What Are My Odds Of Improving A 1-Card Draw To An 8-Low Or Better On A Single Draw?
faqs.a: Holding A Smooth 2-3-4-7-x Draw, Any 5, 6, Or 8 Makes An 8-Low Or 7-Low (12 Outs Out Of 47 Unseen Cards = 25.5%), Plus Any 9 Or T Makes A Playable 9-Low Or T-Low (Another 8 Outs = 42.5% Total Non-Pair/Non-Jack Hit Rate).

A 1-Card Badugi Draw Has At Most 10 Outs Out Of 48 Unseen Cards (13 Cards Of The Missing Suit Minus The 3 Ranks You Already Hold = 10 Outs, Or ~20.8% Per Draw).
Breaking A Pat Rough Badugi (Like K-8-3-2 Rainbow) To Draw 1 Card Toward An 8-Low On The Second Draw Is A High-Level Tactical Play.

faqs.q: Which Hand Wins In Badugi: K-Q-J-T Of Four Different Suits Or As-2h-3d-4d?
faqs.a: K-Q-J-T Of Four Different Suits Wins! Because As-2h-3d-4d Has Two Diamonds, The Higher Diamond (4d) Is Disqualified, Leaving Only A 3-Card Hand (As-2h-3d). Every 4-Card Badugi Beats Every 3-Card Hand.

faqs.q: How Many Outs Does A Three-Card Hand Have To Make A Badugi On One Draw?
faqs.a: If You Hold Three Unpaired Cards Of Three Different Suits (Like As-2h-3d), Only The Fourth Suit (Clubs) Can Make A Badugi, And The Ace, 2, And 3 Of Clubs Would Pair Your Ranks, Leaving Exactly 13 - 3 = 10 Maximum Outs.

faqs.q: When Exactly Do You Discard Your Third Card In Crazy Pineapple?
faqs.a: In Crazy Pineapple, You Discard One Hole Card After All Flop Betting Action Is Complete And Right Before The Dealer Burns And Deals The Turn Card.

glossaryTerms.definition: A 3-Bet Is The First Re-Raise Before The Flop, Made Over An Open Raise. The Blinds Count As The First Bet And The Open As The Second, Which Is Why The Re-Raise Is The Third. A 3-Bet Can Be Made For Value With Strong Hands Or As A Bluff With Hands That Block The Opener's Best Holdings.

A 4-Bet Is A Re-Raise Over A 3-Bet Before The Flop. At Common Stack Depths A 4-Bet Commits A Large Share Of The Effective Stack, So Ranges Become Narrow And Polarized: Premium Pairs And Big Aces For Value, Plus A Few Suited Hands With Blockers As Bluffs. The Next Raise, A 5-Bet, Is Usually All In.

A Cold Call Is A Call Of A Raise By A Player Who Has Put No Voluntary Chips Into The Pot Yet, Such As Flatting An Open From The Button. Cold Calling Invites A Squeeze From The Players Behind And Usually Means Playing Out Of Position Against A Stronger Range, So Solver Strategies Cold Call Far Less Than Most Players Do.

An Isolation Raise Is A Raise Over One Or More Limpers, Sized To Push The Other Players Out So The Raiser Can Play Heads Up Against The Limper, Who Is Often The Weakest Player At The Table. The Usual Size Is The Standard Open Plus One Big Blind For Each Limper Already In The Pot.

RFI, Short For Raise First In, Is The First Voluntary Raise When Every Player Before You Has Folded. RFI Ranges Widen As The Position Gets Later: A Player Under The Gun Opens A Tight Range, While The Button Can Open Close To Half Of All Hands Because Only The Two Blinds Remain To Act Behind.

A Squeeze Is A 3-Bet Made After One Player Has Opened And At Least One Other Player Has Called. It Works Because The Opener Must Worry About The Caller Behind, And The Caller Has Already Shown A Capped Range That Rarely Contains The Strongest Hands. Squeezes Are Usually Sized Larger Than A Normal 3-Bet.

A Backdoor Draw Is A Draw That Needs Both The Turn And The River To Complete, Such As Holding Two Hearts On A Flop With One Heart. It Is Worth Only A Few Percent Of Equity On Its Own, But It Adds Reasons To Bet Or Continue And Gives Bluffs Extra Ways To Improve On Later Streets.

A Barrel Is A Bet On A Later Street After Betting The Street Before. Betting The Flop And The Turn Is A Double Barrel, And Betting All Three Streets Is A Triple Barrel. Good Barrels Continue With Value Hands And With Bluffs That Picked Up Equity Or Blockers, While Giving Up With Hands That Did Neither.

Board Texture Describes How The Community Cards Interact. A Dry Board Such As K72 With Three Suits Offers Few Draws, A Wet Board Is Full Of Straight And Flush Possibilities, And A Monotone Board Shows Three Cards Of One Suit. Texture Decides Which Range It Favors, Which Is Why Bet Sizes And Frequencies Change From Flop To Flop.

A C-Bet, Or Continuation Bet, Is A Flop Bet By The Player Who Made The Last Raise Before The Flop. It Continues The Story The Raise Told. Solver Strategies C-Bet Small And Often On Boards That Favor The Raiser's Range And Bet Less, Or Check, On Boards That Connect Better With The Caller.

A Donk Bet Is A Bet Made Out Of Position Into The Player Who Had The Betting Lead On The Previous Street, Before That Player Can Continue Their Aggression. It Is Usually A Mistake, But A Small Donk Bet Can Be Correct On Turns And Rivers That Improve The Caller's Range Far More Than The Aggressor's.

An Overbet Is Any Bet Larger Than The Pot. It Is Strongest When The Bettor Holds A Clear Nut Advantage And A Polarized Range, Because The Opponent Then Holds Many Medium Hands That Cannot Call Comfortably. Overbets Are Most Common On Turns And Rivers, Where The Board Has Moved In The Bettor's Favor.

A Probe Bet Is A Bet From The Out Of Position Player On The Turn After The In Position Player Checked Back The Flop. The Check Back Weakens That Player's Range, Because Most Strong Hands Would Have Bet, So The Out Of Position Player Can Lead With Value Hands And Draws That Benefit From Building The Pot.

A Semi-Bluff Is A Bet Or Raise With A Hand That Is Probably Behind Now But Has Real Outs To Improve, Such As A Flush Draw Or An Open Ended Straight Draw. It Wins In Two Ways: The Opponent Folds Right Away, Or The Draw Completes. That Combination Makes Semi-Bluffs The Backbone Of Most Balanced Bluffing Ranges.

Slow Playing Means Checking Or Calling With A Very Strong Hand Instead Of Betting Or Raising, So The Opponent Stays In And Keeps Betting. It Works Best On Dry Boards Where Few Cards Can Hurt You And The Opponent Is Likely To Bluff. On Wet Boards And In Multiway Pots It Risks Giving Free Cards That Beat You.

A Thin Value Bet Is A Bet With A Hand That Is Only Slightly Ahead Of The Hands That Will Call, Such As Second Pair Against An Opponent Who Calls With Weaker Pairs. It Earns A Small Profit When Called By Worse And A Small Loss When Called By Better, So Accurate Reads Of The Calling Range Decide Whether It Is Right.

A Trap Is A Line Designed To Induce Bets From An Opponent While Holding A Monster Hand, Usually By Check Calling Or Check Raising Rather Than Leading. It Differs From A Plain Slow Play In Its Aim: The Trapper Wants The Opponent To Bluff Or Bet Worse Hands Into Them, Then Collects The Extra Chips On A Later Street.

A Value Bet Is A Bet Made Because Worse Hands Will Call It Often Enough To Show A Profit. The Test Is Simple: If The Opponent Calls, Are You Ahead Of Most Of The Hands They Call With? Value Bets Pay For Bluffs In A Balanced Strategy, And Missing Them Costs More Money Than Most Players Realize.

A Wet Board Is A Flop Or Turn With Many Straight And Flush Possibilities, Such As J T 9 With Two Hearts. Equities Run Closer On Wet Boards, So Strong Hands Bet Larger To Charge Draws, And Ranges Change Sharply From Street To Street. The Opposite Is A Dry Board, Where Few Draws Exist And Small Bets Are Common.

A Combo Is One Specific Way To Hold A Starting Hand, Counting Suits. Every Pocket Pair Has 6 Combos, Every Suited Hand Has 4 And Every Offsuit Hand Has 12, For 1,326 Starting Combos In Total. Counting Combos, And Removing Those Your Own Cards Block, Is How Players Estimate How Often An Opponent Holds A Given Hand.

Expected Value, Or EV, Is The Average Result Of A Decision If It Could Be Repeated Many Times. Each Possible Outcome Is Multiplied By Its Probability And The Results Are Added Together. A Positive EV Play Earns Over Time Even When It Loses On A Given Hand, Which Is Why Good Players Judge Decisions By EV Rather Than Results.

Equity Is Your Share Of The Pot Based On How Often Your Hand Would Win If All Remaining Cards Were Dealt With No Further Betting. A Hand With 40 Percent Equity In A 100 Chip Pot Owns 40 Chips Of It On Average. Equity Against A Whole Range, Rather Than One Hand, Is What Drives Sound Decisions.

ICM, The Independent Chip Model, Converts Tournament Chip Stacks Into Shares Of The Remaining Prize Pool. Because Chips Lost Hurt More Than Chips Won Help Once Payouts Are Close, ICM Tells Players To Tighten Their Calling Ranges Near The Bubble And At Final Tables. It Is The Standard Tool For Tournament Deals And Late Stage Push And Fold Decisions.

Implied Odds Are The Chips You Expect To Win On Later Streets When Your Draw Completes, Beyond What Is Already In The Pot. They Justify Calling With Hands Such As Small Pairs Or Suited Connectors When The Immediate Pot Odds Are Too Thin, Provided Stacks Are Deep And The Opponent Will Pay Off When You Hit.

Minimum Defense Frequency, Or MDF, Is The Share Of Your Range You Must Continue With So That An Opponent's Bluff Cannot Profit Automatically. It Equals The Pot Divided By The Pot Plus The Bet, So Facing A Pot Sized Bet You Defend At Least Half Your Range. It Is A Guideline, Not A Rule, Against Opponents Who Rarely Bluff.

Outs Are The Unseen Cards That Improve Your Hand To The Likely Winner. A Flush Draw Has Nine Outs And An Open Ended Straight Draw Has Eight. A Quick Estimate Of Your Chance To Hit Is Outs Times Four On The Flop, With Two Cards To Come, Or Outs Times Two On The Turn With One Card Left.

Pot Odds Compare The Size Of A Call With The Pot You Could Win. Divide The Call By The Total Pot After You Call To Find The Equity You Need: Calling 50 Into A Pot That Will Be 150 Needs 33 Percent. If Your Equity Is Higher Than That Break Even Point, The Call Makes Money Over Time.

Reverse Implied Odds Are The Chips You Expect To Lose On Later Streets When You Make Your Hand But An Opponent Has Made A Better One. Dominated Hands Such As Weak Aces And Low Flush Draws Carry Heavy Reverse Implied Odds, Because They Often Win Small Pots And Lose Big Ones, Which Makes Them Worse Than Their Raw Equity Suggests.

SPR, The Stack To Pot Ratio, Is The Effective Stack Divided By The Pot At The Start Of A Street, Usually The Flop. A Low SPR, Below About Three, Means Top Pair Is Often Worth Getting All In. A High SPR, Above Ten, Rewards Hands That Can Make The Nuts And Punishes One Pair Hands That Overcommit.

Variance Is The Spread Of Results Around A Player's Expected Value. High Variance Games Such As Tournaments And Pot Limit Omaha Produce Long Losing And Winning Stretches Even For Skilled Players. Understanding Variance Keeps Decisions Tied To Expected Value, And It Is Why A Large Sample Of Hands Is Needed Before Judging Any Strategy.

VPIP, Short For Voluntarily Put Money In Pot, Is The Share Of Hands A Player Calls Or Raises Before The Flop. Posting A Blind Does Not Count, Only Voluntary Chips Do. A VPIP Near 20 To 25 Percent At A Full Ring Cash Table Is Typical Of A Solid Regular, While A VPIP Above 40 Percent Usually Marks A Loose Player.

A Blocker Is A Card In Your Hand That Reduces The Number Of Combos Of A Particular Hand Your Opponent Can Hold. Holding The Ace Of Hearts On A Board With Three Hearts Means The Opponent Cannot Have The Nut Flush. Blockers Guide The Choice Of Which Hands To Bluff With And Which Marginal Hands Can Call.

Exploitative Play Deliberately Departs From A Balanced Strategy To Win More Against A Specific Opponent's Mistakes, Such As Bluffing More Against A Player Who Folds Too Often. It Can Earn More Than Game Theory Optimal Play Against Weak Opponents, But It Opens You To Counter Exploitation If The Read Is Wrong Or The Opponent Adjusts.

Fold Equity Is The Extra Value A Bet Or Raise Gains From The Chance That The Opponent Folds. It Equals How Often They Fold Multiplied By The Pot You Win When They Do. Fold Equity Is Why A Semi-Bluff Can Be Profitable When Calling Cannot, And Why Short Stacks Lose Much Of Their Bluffing Power.

Frequency Is How Often A Player Takes An Action In A Given Spot Across Their Whole Range, For Example Betting 65 Percent Of The Time On A Particular Flop. Solvers Express Strategy As Frequencies Rather Than Fixed Rules, And Matching Sensible Frequencies Is What Keeps A Player Hard To Read And Hard To Exploit.

GTO, Or Game Theory Optimal, Describes A Strategy That Cannot Be Exploited, Because No Opposing Strategy Can Win Against It In The Long Run. In Poker It Approximates A Nash Equilibrium Computed By A Solver. Players Study GTO To Build A Sound Baseline, Then Adjust Away From It To Exploit The Specific Mistakes Of Real Opponents.

In Position, Or IP, Means Acting After Your Opponent On Every Postflop Street. The Player In Position Sees What The Opponent Does Before Deciding, Controls The Size Of The Pot And Can Take Free Cards. The Dealer Button Is Always In Position After The Flop, Which Is Why Late Positions Play More Hands Profitably.

A Linear Range, Also Called A Merged Range, Is A Betting Range Built From The Strongest Hands Downward With No Gap, Such As Every Pair From Aces Down To A Middle Pair. It Suits Spots Where Many Worse Hands Will Call. The Contrast Is A Polarized Range, Which Skips The Middle And Bets Only Very Strong Hands And Bluffs.

A Mixed Strategy Plays The Same Hand In Different Ways At Set Frequencies, For Example Betting A Hand 60 Percent Of The Time And Checking It 40 Percent. Solvers Produce Mixed Strategies When Two Actions Have Nearly Equal Expected Value, And Mixing Keeps Each Line Balanced So An Opponent Cannot Read The Hand From The Action.

A Nash Equilibrium Is A Set Of Strategies In Which No Player Can Gain By Changing Their Own Strategy While The Others Stay The Same. In Two Player Zero Sum Games Such As Heads Up Poker, An Equilibrium Strategy Is Unexploitable. Poker Solvers Approximate It Closely, And That Output Is What Players Call A GTO Strategy.

Nodelocking Is A Solver Technique That Fixes One Player's Strategy At A Decision Point, For Example Forcing A Player To Bet Too Often, And Then Recomputes The Best Response For Everyone Else. It Shows How The Optimal Counter Strategy Changes Against A Real Tendency, Which Makes It The Bridge Between GTO Study And Exploitative Play.

Nut Advantage Means One Player's Range Holds More Of The Strongest Possible Hands On The Current Board Than The Opponent's Range Does. It Is Different From Range Advantage, Which Compares Average Strength. A Player With A Nut Advantage Can Use Large Bets And Overbets, Because The Opponent Rarely Holds Hands Strong Enough To Punish Them.

Out Of Position, Or OOP, Means Acting Before Your Opponent On Each Postflop Street. The Out Of Position Player Gives Information Away First And Has Less Control Over The Size Of The Pot, Which Lowers The Value Of Every Hand. The Blinds Play Most Pots Out Of Position, Which Is Why They Defend Tighter Than Their Price Suggests.

A Polarized Range Is Made Of Very Strong Hands And Bluffs, With Few Medium Strength Hands In Between. Polarized Ranges Pair With Large Bets And Overbets, Because Strong Hands Want The Pot To Grow And Bluffs Need The Fold Equity. The Medium Hands That Are Left Out Are Checked, Where They Keep Their Showdown Value.

A Range Is The Full Set Of Hands A Player Could Hold In A Given Spot, Based On Their Position And Every Action So Far. Strong Players Think In Ranges Rather Than Single Hands, Because Opponents Act With Many Hands In The Same Way. Reading A Range Means Narrowing It Street By Street As New Actions Arrive.

Range Advantage Means One Player's Whole Range Has More Equity On The Current Board Than The Opponent's Range. The Preflop Raiser Usually Has It On High Card Flops Such As A K 4. The Player With Range Advantage Can Bet Often With A Small Size, While The Other Player Defends More Carefully And Bets Rarely.

A Sizing Tell Is Information Leaked By The Size Of A Bet, Such As A Player Who Bets Small With Medium Hands And Large Only With The Nuts. Opponents Who Notice Can Fold And Raise Accurately Against Each Size. Balanced Strategies Prevent The Leak By Betting A Mix Of Strong Hands And Bluffs With Every Size They Use.

Tilt Is An Emotional State In Which Frustration, Anger Or Overconfidence Leads A Player To Make Worse Decisions Than Usual, Such As Calling Too Wide After A Bad Beat. It Is One Of The Largest Leaks In Poker. Common Remedies Include Stop Loss Limits, Short Breaks And Reviewing Decisions Rather Than Results After A Session.

Under-Defense Is Folding Too Often When Facing Bets, Which Lets An Opponent Profit By Betting Any Two Cards. A Player Defending Well Below The Minimum Defense Frequency In Common Spots Is Easy To Exploit With Bluffs. The Fix Is To Continue With More Hands That Have Equity Or Blockers, Not To Call Everything.

Villain Is Poker Slang For The Opponent In A Hand Being Discussed, While Hero Is The Player Telling The Story. The Terms Are Neutral Labels, Not Insults, And Appear In Almost Every Hand History And Strategy Forum. A Hand Review Might Say Villain Opens From The Cutoff And Hero Defends From The Big Blind.

Blinds Are Forced Bets Posted Before The Cards Are Dealt By The Two Players To The Left Of The Button: The Small Blind And The Big Blind, Which Is Usually Twice As Large. Blinds Create A Pot Worth Fighting For On Every Hand. Stakes Are Named After Them, So A 1/2 Game Has A 1 Small Blind And A 2 Big Blind.

The Dealer Button Is The Marker That Shows Which Player Acts Last In Each Betting Round After The Flop. It Moves One Seat To The Left After Every Hand, And The Blinds Are Posted By The Two Players To Its Left. The Button Is The Most Profitable Seat At The Table Because It Plays Every Postflop Street In Position.

The Effective Stack Is The Smaller Of The Stacks Between Two Players In A Hand, Because Nobody Can Win Or Lose More Than That Amount From The Other. If One Player Has 300 Chips And The Other 80, The Effective Stack Is 80. Strategy Depends On Effective Stacks, Not The Size Of Either Player's Own Stack.

Rake Is The Fee A Card Room Or Club Takes From Each Pot Or Tournament Entry To Pay For Running The Game, Usually A Percentage Of The Pot Up To A Cap. Rake Is The Main Way A Poker Operator Earns Revenue. In Play Credit Games, Rake Is Taken In Chips That Have No Cash Value.

Showdown Is The Moment After The Final Betting Round When The Remaining Players Reveal Their Cards And The Best Five Card Hand Wins The Pot. The Last Player To Bet Or Raise On The River Shows First. A Player Who Cannot Win May Muck, Meaning Fold The Hand Face Down, Without Showing It.

A Poker Union Is An Alliance Of Private Online Poker Clubs That Share One Pool Of Tables, So Members Of Every Club In The Union Can Play Each Other And Games Run At More Stakes And Hours. A Union Sets Shared Rules And Fees. On Smarter.Poker Unions Use Club Chips, Which Are Play Credits With No Cash Value.

A Club Agent Is A Person Who Recruits Players Into A Private Online Poker Club And Looks After Them There, Managing Their Chip Requests And Questions For The Club Owner. In The Wider Industry Agents Are Often Paid A Share Of The Rake Their Players Generate. On Smarter.Poker Agent Tools Manage Club Chips, Which Have No Cash Value.

Rakeback Is A Rebate Of Part Of The Rake A Player Pays, Returned By The Room, Club Or Agent As A Loyalty Incentive, Often As A Fixed Percentage Each Week. It Lowers The Effective Cost Of Playing. On Smarter.Poker There Is No Real-Money Gambling, So Any Rebate Is In Club Chips Or Rewards With No Cash Value.

On Smarter.Poker, Club Chips And Diamonds Are Two Separate Currencies. Club Chips Are Play Credits A Club Issues For Its Own Tables, With No Cash Value. Diamonds Are A Promotional Rewards Currency Used Across The Platform. Neither Can Be Cashed Out, And There Is No Real-Money Gambling On The Platform.

Settlement Is The Periodic Reconciliation Of Chip Balances In A Club Or Union, Usually Weekly, When Wins, Losses, Rake Shares And Agent Balances Are Totaled And Zeroed For The New Period. Real-Money Clubs Settle In Cash Outside The App. On Smarter.Poker Settlement Only Reconciles Club Chips, Which Are Play Credits With No Cash Value.

A Club ID Is The Unique Number Or Code That Identifies A Private Online Poker Club Inside A Poker App. Players Enter The Club ID To Find The Club And Request To Join, And The Owner Or An Agent Approves The Request. Sharing A Club ID Is How Private Clubs Invite New Members Without A Public Listing.

GPS And IP Restriction Is A Table Security Setting That Blocks Players Who Are Physically Close Together, Or Who Share An Internet Address, From Sitting At The Same Table. It Targets Collusion, Where Friends In One Room Share Hole Cards Or Team Up Against Others. Club Owners Switch It On Per Table When Creating A Game.

Insurance Is An Optional Side Bet Offered In Some Club Games When Players Are All In Before The River. The Player Ahead Can Pay A Premium To Be Paid Back If An Opponent's Out Lands, Which Reduces Variance On Big All In Pots. The Price Is Set From The Number Of Outs, And The House Keeps The Edge.

Run It Twice Is An Agreement Between All In Players To Deal The Remaining Board Cards Two Times And Split The Pot, With Half Going To The Winner Of Each Run. It Does Not Change Anyone's Expected Value, But It Reduces Variance, So A Big Pot Is Less Likely To Be Decided Entirely By One Card.

A Time Bank Is A Reserve Of Extra Seconds An Online Player Can Draw On After The Normal Action Clock Runs Out, For A Difficult Decision. Once Used, The Extra Time Is Gone Until It Refills, Often After A Set Number Of Hands. Time Banks Keep Games Moving While Still Allowing Time To Think In Big Spots.

A Straddle Is An Optional Blind Bet, Usually Twice The Big Blind, Posted Before The Cards Are Dealt By The Player To The Left Of The Big Blind. It Doubles The Stakes For That Hand, And The Straddler Acts Last Before The Flop. Many Rooms And Clubs Also Allow Button Or Mississippi Straddles Under House Rules.

A Bomb Pot Is A Special Hand In Which Every Player Puts An Agreed Amount Into The Pot Before The Deal And The Hand Skips Preflop Betting, Going Straight To The Flop. Bomb Pots Create Large Multiway Pots And Are Often Played With A Double Board, Where The Pot Is Split Between The Winners Of Each Board.

A Waitlist Is The Queue A Poker Room Keeps For Each Game, Such As 1/3 No Limit Hold'em, So Players Are Seated In Order As Seats Open. Players Can Join For Several Games At Once And Are Called By Name When A Seat Is Ready. Remote Waitlists Let Players Join From A Phone Before Arriving At The Room.

A Must-Move Table Is A Second Table Of The Same Game That Feeds A Main Table. Players Start At The Must-Move Table And Are Moved To The Main Game In Order As Seats Open There. It Keeps The Main Table Full, Protects It From Breaking, And Lets A Room Start A New Game While The Waitlist Is Still Long.

Table Balancing Is Moving Players Between Tables So Each Table In A Tournament Or Cash Game Stays Close To The Same Number Of Players. In Tournaments, The Tournament Director Moves A Player From The Fullest Table To The Shortest, Usually Into The Equivalent Position, And Breaks Tables As The Field Shrinks Toward The Final Table.

A Chip-Up, Also Called A Color Up, Is When A Tournament Removes Its Smallest Chip Denomination Once The Blinds No Longer Need It And Exchanges Those Chips For Larger Ones. Leftover Odd Chips Are Settled By A Chip Race, Dealing One Card Per Odd Chip, So A Player Can Never Be Eliminated By The Chip-Up Itself.

A Comp, Short For Complimentary, Is A Reward A Poker Room Or Casino Gives Players For Time Played, Such As Food Credits Or Points Toward Merchandise. Comps Are Usually Earned Per Hour Of Live Play And Tracked On A Player Card. Each Venue Sets Its Own Earning Rate, Redemption Rules And Expiry Policy For Comps.

A High Hand Promotion Pays A Bonus To The Player Who Makes The Best Qualifying Hand During A Set Period, Such As The Highest Hand Of Each Hour Where Quads Or Better Qualify. Many Rooms Require Both Hole Cards To Play And The Hand To Reach Showdown. The Prize Is Usually Funded From A Small Drop Taken From Each Pot.

A Bad Beat Jackpot Is A Progressive Prize Paid When A Very Strong Hand, Such As Four Jacks Or Better, Loses At Showdown To An Even Stronger Hand. The Losing Player Usually Takes The Largest Share, With The Winner And The Rest Of The Table Splitting The Remainder. It Is Funded By A Small Drop Taken From Each Qualifying Pot.

A Mystery Bounty Is A Tournament Format Where Knocking Out An Opponent After The Bounty Phase Begins Awards A Sealed Envelope Or Random Prize Draw Instead Of A Fixed Cash Amount. Prizes Range From One Minimum Bounty Up To A Jackpot Worth Ten Percent Or More Of The Total Prize Pool, Dramatically Increasing Late-Stage Shoving And Calling Incentives.

A Progressive Knockout, Or PKO, Is A Bounty Tournament Where Half Of An Eliminated Player's Bounty Is Awarded Immediately To The Winner Of The Pot And The Other Half Is Added Onto The Winner's Own Head. As The Tournament Reaches The Final Table, Surviving Players Carry Enormous Bounties That Outweigh Standard Ladder Payout Jumps.

A Block Bet Is A Small Out-Of-Position Bet, Typically Twenty To Thirty Percent Of The Pot, Made On The Turn Or River With A Medium-Strength Hand To Set Your Own Price For Showdown And Prevent The In-Position Opponent From Betting A Much Larger Amount. To Stay Unexploitable, Players Balance Block Bets With A Few Nutted Traps And Bluffs.

A Double-Board Bomb Pot Is A Live And Club Game Variant Where Every Seated Player Posts An Agreed Ante Before The Deal, Preflop Betting Is Skipped, And Two Separate Flops, Turns And Rivers Are Dealt Simultaneously. Half The Pot Is Awarded To The Best Hand On The Top Board And Half To The Bottom Board.

A Capped Range Is A Range Of Hands That Contains No Nutted Or Very Strong Holdings Because The Player Previously Passed Up An Opportunity To Raise Or Three-Bet. When A Player Calls Preflop And Check-Calls Twice On A Dry Board, Their Range Is Usually Capped At One Pair, Making Them Vulnerable To Large Polarized River Overbets.

Geometric Sizing, Often Called Equal-Percentage Betting, Is Calculating The Exact Bet Percentage Of The Pot Needed Across The Remaining Streets So That All Remaining Effective Chips Go In On The River Using The Same Fraction Each Street. Solvers Frequently Select Geometric Sizings When Pressing A Strong Nut Advantage With Polarized Value And Bluff Ranges.
